title: The remote passed pawn: bring the king first
outcomes: Explains why the remote passed pawn waits: the king does its work first, because the enemy king cannot catch the pawn in time
Decides in a given ending whether to push the remote passed pawn now or move the king first
Recognises a position with no passed pawn, where the idea does not apply

steps.text: A passed pawn **far from the kings** is a *remote passed pawn*. The enemy king cannot catch it in time, so it ties his king down while your own king does the other work. Push it too early and his king can take your other pawns and come back in time. Watch Black: king first, then the pawn.

steps.caption: Black to move. Kxd4 first keeps d5 safe; h5 at once lets White take d5 and catch up.

steps.text: **Conditions.** Pushing is not wrong in itself. If the pawn push wins ground at once, push; if your king still has work to do, move the king first. Rule of thumb: ask what each side's king can reach while the pawn runs. And check the pawns first: with no passed pawn there is no decoy at all. Predict the three cases.

steps.title: One feature at a time
steps.prompt: Three positions with Black to move, all built from the first. In the second only Black's king has moved (g4 to h5); in the third the b-pawn is gone. Which advice fits each: push the passed pawn now, move the king first, or there is no passed pawn?
Before each answer: did you ask what the kings could reach while the pawn ran, or did you push because the pawn was passed? Which did you do?
